author: thomas_hardy
text:
A Bough from an apple tree, half-dead in summer, had
Been shaken by a breeze. Its leaves, that were dead to all
But one or two sweet bees, made now a kind of chorus
For them. The bees began to buzz within their cover,
And then they sung; but not like those who are singing
In praise of Spring or Love,--not even as a choir
Of happy birds would have done it,--but with sadness,--
As if their voice complained of its own uselessness,
Or seemed too strong to bear its burden of sound.

One of those dusty mornings,
When our long-tailed hearts were full,
And we stood like shadows under a trellis
Of white-and-black-and -grey clouds—

The sunlight went drifting down to us;
It touched the dark hair on your face,
Made the black smoke from the chimney’s crown
To be grey-white as ash in the grass . . .

My heart is still filled with that sunshine!

author: stephen_crane
text:
Little

I was once a lonely child in my play-time,
And I wandered into an old wood one day;
My eyes were fixed on a bird that flew away,--
“Oh! I shall catch it,” said I to myself.
A squirrel chattered close at my side with glee--
It ran across me without a glance or cry--
The trees were bare, but two leaves upon them lay,--
There they still are; their colour is like clay.

Meritocracy is a belief that one's position in life should be determined by his or her abilities. People with talent, determination, and hard work will rise to their proper place in society. A meritocratic system allows each person freedom to pursue his own goals without government intervention. The system rewards individual accomplishment. In practice, however, a true meritocracy has never existed, because of human nature, which inclines individuals toward favoritism and prejudice against those who are different from themselves. An aristocracy (or oligarchy) based on wealth and power may arise in an attempt to control such tendencies.

author: vanburen
text: When a government fails to maintain its integrity within the nation, it risks being overthrown by its citizens. Domestic problems can lead to social unrest and political instability, ultimately resulting in loss of power by the ruling class. This often leads to violence between civilians and law enforcement officials, which puts society in jeopardy. The consequences of ignoring internal issues can become severe when citizens resort to violent means against the state authority.

author: buchanan
text:
Fellow-Citizens of the Senate and House of Representatives:
I shall be exceedingly happy to see the occasion afforded me this day to return my best thanks to you for your kindness in referring the Executive measures of our government under their consideration; and I am gratified that so much has been done by both Houses which will give pleasure to all who have a right to claim it from us, at home or abroad. My first duty is, therefore, to say, with profound gratitude to Heaven, "Thanks to God for protection." We are, indeed, indebted for blessings unspeakable to His care.
